sections.title: At Work
sections.content: An office brings its own cast — the boss, the colleagues, the building — and a handful of verbs you can build already: ayudar, descansar, aprender, explicar. Two are irregular in the yo form only: 'conocer' becomes 'conozco', and 'empezar' changes its stem like querer, 'empiezo'.

items.spanish: El lunes Carlos empieza un nuevo trabajo en una oficina.
items.english: On Monday Carlos starts a new job in an office.

items.spanish: Su jefe le enseña el edificio y le explica sus tareas.
items.english: His boss shows him the building and explains his tasks.

items.spanish: Paso la mañana leyendo documentos y en una reunión.
items.english: I spend the morning reading documents and in a meeting.

items.spanish: Todos desean mucha suerte a Carlos.
items.english: Everyone wishes Carlos lots of luck.

sections.content: 'El compañero' is any colleague or classmate — a workmate, not a partner. And 'el jefe' has a feminine form, 'la jefa', which you will hear far more often than the textbooks suggest.
